subject: Chemistry
title: Chemistry Daily Practice
scope: S4 + S5 revision (mole, acids & bases, redox, electrolysis)
keyPoints: **Mole:** $n = \frac{m}{M}$; $c = \frac{n}{V}$ ($V$ in dm³); molar volume of gas at r.t.p. = 24.0 dm³ mol⁻¹.
**Titration:** use the mole ratio from the balanced equation: $n_{\text{acid}} : n_{\text{base}}$ = coefficient ratio.
**pH:** $\text{pH} = -\log[\text{H}^+]$. Strong acid fully ionises; weak acid partly ionises, so at equal concentration it has higher pH and reacts more slowly (same total moles of H⁺ available).
**Redox:** oxidation = loss of electrons / increase in oxidation number; reducing agent gets oxidised.
**Electrolysis:** cathode = reduction, anode = oxidation. Preferential discharge depends on (1) position in E.C.S., (2) concentration of ions, (3) nature of electrodes.
**Answer pattern (electrolysis):** name the ion discharged + reason (“Cl⁻ is discharged in preference to OH⁻ because [Cl⁻] ≫ [OH⁻]”) + half equation + observation.

examples.title: 例题 1 (mole / gas volume)
examples.question: 2.4 g of Mg reacts with excess dilute HCl. Find the volume of H₂ at r.t.p.
examples.solution:
Mg + 2HCl → MgCl₂ + H₂
$n(\text{Mg}) = 2.4/24.3 = 0.0988$ mol $\Rightarrow n(\text{H}_2) = 0.0988$ mol.
$V = 0.0988 \times 24.0 = 2.37$ dm³.

examples.title: 例题 2 (titration)
examples.question: 20.0 cm³ of NaOH needs 16.0 cm³ of 0.100 M H₂SO₄. Find [NaOH].

examples.title: 例题 3 (pH, strong vs weak)
examples.question: Compare 0.1 M HNO₃ and 0.1 M HCOOH.
examples.solution: HNO₃ is a strong acid, fully ionised: [H⁺] = 0.1, pH = 1. HCOOH is weak, partly ionised, so [H⁺] < 0.1 M and pH > 1.

examples.title: 例题 4 (redox)
examples.question: In Zn + Cu²⁺ → Zn²⁺ + Cu, state the reducing agent.
examples.solution: Zn: O.N. 0 → +2, loses electrons, is oxidised, so Zn is the reducing agent.

examples.title: 例题 5 (electrolysis explanation)
examples.question: Dilute H₂SO₄ is electrolysed with carbon electrodes. Anode product?
examples.solution:
Ions at anode: SO₄²⁻, OH⁻. OH⁻ is lower in the E.C.S., so it is preferentially discharged:
4OH⁻ → O₂ + 2H₂O + 4e⁻
Colourless gas bubbles; oxygen formed.

questions.solution: Same moles of acid give the same volume of H₂; the weak acid has lower [H⁺], so a slower rate and higher pH.

questions.source: Adapted from DSE Paper 1B titration pattern
questions.stem: 2.65 g of anhydrous Na₂CO₃ was dissolved and made up to 250.0 cm³. 25.0 cm³ of this solution needed 22.50 cm³ of dilute HCl (methyl orange).

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Write the equation for the reaction.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: State the colour change at end point.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Calculate the concentration of the HCl.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text: Name the apparatus used to measure exactly 25.0 cm³ of solution.

questions.source: Adapted from DSE Paper 1B electrolysis pattern
questions.stem: Dilute CuSO₄ solution is electrolysed using copper electrodes.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Write the half equation at each electrode.
parts.answer: Cathode: Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Cu; anode: Cu → Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ (2)

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: State the change in mass of each electrode.
parts.answer: Cathode gains mass; anode loses mass (by the same amount) (2)

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Explain why the blue colour of the solution stays the same.
parts.answer: Rate of Cu²⁺ formed at anode = rate of Cu²⁺ discharged at cathode (1), so [Cu²⁺] stays constant (1).

parts.label: (d)
parts.text: If the copper anode is replaced by a carbon anode, state and explain the observation at the anode, and the change in colour of the solution.
parts.answer: Colourless gas bubbles (1); OH⁻ preferentially discharged over SO₄²⁻ as it is lower in E.C.S. (1), 4OH⁻ → O₂ + 2H₂O + 4e⁻; blue colour fades (1) because Cu²⁺ is removed at the cathode and not replaced (1).

questions.source: Adapted from DSE Paper 1B redox/reactivity pattern
questions.stem: Excess zinc powder is added to 50.0 cm³ of 0.200 M CuSO₄ solution.

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: Reddish-brown solid forms; blue solution fades/becomes colourless (2)

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Write the ionic equation and identify the oxidising agent.
parts.answer: Zn + Cu²⁺ → Zn²⁺ + Cu (1); oxidising agent Cu²⁺ (1)

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Calculate the mass of copper formed. (Cu = 63.5)

parts.label: (d)
parts.text: Explain, in terms of electrons, why zinc is more reactive than copper.
parts.answer: Zn loses electrons more readily than Cu (1)

parts.label: (e)
parts.text: Suggest why the temperature of the mixture rises.

parts.label: (f)
parts.text: State whether the reaction would occur if silver were used instead of zinc. Explain.
parts.answer: No (1): Ag is less reactive than Cu / lower in the reactivity series, so cannot displace Cu (1).
